mainTopic: Whether a plain נזירות lasts 30 days (רב מתנא) or 29 days (בר פדא), tested against the wording and rulings of the משנה.
overview: Earlier on the דף, רב מתנא said a plain נזירות lasts 30 days, and בר פדא said it lasts 29 days, based on how many times the word נזיר or נזר appears in the פרשה. First בר פדא defends his count: at least one of those words is free just for counting, so all of them count, even the ones that also teach other lessons. Then the גמרא tests both views against the משנה. The משנה says a plain נזירות is 'thirty days', and בר פדא explains that day 30 is included because the נזיר shaves and brings his קרבנות then. Another משנה says the נזיר shaves on day 31. בר פדא answers from the end of that משנה, which says shaving on day 30 still counts. That same line now seems to be a problem for רב מתנא, and he answers with the rule מקצת היום ככולו, that part of a day counts like the whole day. When the משנה says someone who vowed 'thirty days' cannot shave on day 30, the גמרא explains that he said 'complete' days. Finally, the גמרא brings the case of two נזירויות, with shaving on day 31 and day 61, which fits רב מתנא. The challenge to בר פדא from that case continues on the next amud.

steps.title: בר פדא defends his word-count
steps.stepSummary: בר פדא answers that even if some of the words are used for דרשות, at least one is free just for counting, so all of them count toward the number.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר פדא could say to you: is there not at least one of these words that is not used for a דרשה? Since that one is there for the count, all of them are also there for the count.
steps.whatsHappening: בר פדא answers the objection that the word נזיר in the פרשה is needed for other lessons, so it cannot be used to count days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection said: those words already teach other הלכות, so you cannot count them. בר פדא answers that at least one appearance teaches nothing else, which shows the Torah meant the words to be counted. Once that is clear, every appearance counts toward the number, even the ones that also teach a separate דרשה.

keyTerms.meaning: is there not / there is not
for a דרשה, a lesson learned from the words
for the count, to give a number

steps.confusionAlert: בר פדא is not saying the words teach no lessons. He agrees they teach other הלכות. He is saying they ALSO count toward the number of days.

phrases.english: And bar Padda could say to you:
Is there not one of them
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the times the word נזיר or נזר appears in the פרשה of נזיר.

phrases.english: that is not for an exposition?
Rather, since that one is for the count,
all of them are also for the count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection from the earlier part of the דף that the words are needed for other דרשות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A word can serve two purposes: it teaches its own lesson and also counts toward the number.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A word already used for a דרשה cannot also be counted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since at least one appearance is free for counting, all of the appearances count, even while teaching other lessons.

steps.title: The משנה says thirty days
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a plain נזירות is 30 days. That fits רב מתנא but seems to contradict בר פדא's 29.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: a plain נזירות is thirty days. This works well for רב מתנא, but it is difficult for בר פדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges בר פדא from the wording of the משנה, which says 'thirty days'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מתנא holds 30 days, so the משנה matches him exactly. בר פדא holds 29 days, so the משנה's number 'thirty' seems to go against him.

keyTerms.meaning: a plain נזירות, taken on with no length stated

phrases.english: We learned: an unspecified naziriteship is thirty days.
Granted, according to Rav Mattana it works out well,
but according to bar Padda it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having defended בר פדא's source, the גמרא now tests his view against the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: בר פדא's view that a plain נזירות is 29 days.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly says thirty days, not 29.

steps.title: Why the משנה says thirty
steps.stepSummary: בר פדא explains that the משנה says 30 because on day 30 the נזיר shaves and brings his קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר פדא could say to you: since there is the thirtieth day, on which he shaves and brings his קרבנות, the תנא said thirty.
steps.whatsHappening: בר פדא explains why the משנה says 'thirty' even though the real נזירות is only 29 days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בר פדא's view, the core נזירות is 29 days. Day 30 is the day the נזיר shaves and brings his קרבנות, so it is still part of the process. That is why the משנה can call the whole thing thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: he shaves (his hair, at the end of the נזירות)
his קרבנות, the offerings brought at the end of the נזירות

phrases.english: Bar Padda could say to you:
Since there is the thirtieth day
on which he shaves and brings his offerings,
because of this the tanna taught thirty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה's wording 'thirty days'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the number in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Thirty days' means the נזירות itself lasts 30 days.
steps.terutzMaskana: The נזירות itself is 29 days, and day 30 is counted because the shaving and the קרבנות happen then.

steps.title: Shaving on day thirty-one
steps.stepSummary: Another משנה says the נזיר shaves on day 31. That fits רב מתנא but seems to contradict בר פדא, who would expect shaving on day 30.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: one who said 'I am a נזיר' shaves on the thirty-first day. This works well for רב מתנא, but it is difficult for בר פדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second challenge to בר פדא from another משנה. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב מתנא, the 30 days must be complete first, so shaving on day 31 makes sense. For בר פדא, the נזירות ends after 29 days, so the shaving should be on day 30. His previous answer even assumed shaving happens on day 30.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I am hereby a נזיר', the words of the vow

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge is sharper than the first one. בר פדא's previous answer relied on shaving happening on day 30, but this משנה says day 31.

phrases.english: We learned: one who said 'I am hereby a nazirite'
phrases.notes: This is a different משנה, found later in the מסכת (דף טז).

phrases.english: shaves on the thirty-first day.
Granted, according to Rav Mattana it works out well,
but according to bar Padda it is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: מִי שֶׁאָמַר הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר מְגַלֵּחַ יוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים וְאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to בר פדא, which also undercuts the claim in the previous answer that shaving is on day 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: בר פדא's 29-day view and his claim that shaving happens on day 30.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the נזירות ends after 29 days, the shaving should be on day 30, yet the משנה says day 31.

steps.title: בר פדא points to the end of the משנה, which allows shaving on day 30
steps.stepSummary: בר פדא answers that the end of the same משנה says shaving on day 30 is valid, which fits his view. The day-31 rule is only the ideal way, because a plain vow is treated like a vow of 'complete' days.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר פדא can say: look at the end of the משנה. If he shaved on day 30, it counts. So the end clause actually supports me. As for the first clause (shave on day 31), that is because he is treated as if he had said 'thirty complete days.'
steps.whatsHappening: בר פדא defends himself against the day-31 challenge by quoting the next line of the same משנה, which says shaving on day 30 is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If shaving on day 30 counts after the fact, then the נזירות must already be over by day 30, which fits בר פדא's 29 days. The day-31 rule is only the best way to do it, because חכמים treated a plain vow like someone who said 'שלימין' (complete days).

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read) the end clause of the source
The first clause of the source

phrases.english: Bar Padda could say to you:
Read the end clause of that Mishnah:
If he shaved on the thirtieth day, he has fulfilled his obligation.
phrases.notes: This is the very same משנה from step 4, just the line after the day-31 rule.

phrases.english: Rather, the end clause actually supports him,
and the first clause: he is treated like one who said "complete" days.
phrases.notes: So the day-31 rule is only the ideal way to do it, not the actual length of the נזירות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ בַּר פְּדָא, אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the משנה: the end clause gives the basic law, and the first clause gives the ideal practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Shaving on day 31 shows that the נזירות lasts a full 30 days
steps.terutzMaskana: Shaving on day 30 is valid, so the נזירות lasts 29 days. Day 31 is only the ideal, because a plain vow is treated like a vow of 'complete' days

steps.title: The end of the משנה now seems to be a problem for רב מתנא
steps.stepSummary: If shaving on day 30 counts, that seems to contradict רב מתנא, who says the נזירות lasts a full 30 days.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for רב מתנא, the end clause is a problem!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same end clause against רב מתנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב מתנא, the 30th day is still part of the נזירות. So how can shaving on that day count, when the נזירות is not over yet?

phrases.english: But for Rav Mattana, the end clause is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the source that helped בר פדא in step 5 as a challenge to רב מתנא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מתנא's view that a plain נזירות is 30 full days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If day 30 is still inside the נזירות, shaving on that day should not count. Yet the משנה says it does.

steps.title: רב מתנא: part of a day counts like the whole day
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנא holds מקצת היום ככולו. Once day 30 has begun, it counts as complete, so shaving then is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that part of the day is like the whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב מתנא with the rule that a small part of a day counts as the full day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נזירות really is 30 days. But as soon as day 30 starts, it counts as if the whole day has passed, so the 30 days are already finished and shaving is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Part of a day counts like the whole day

steps.whyThisMatters: מקצת היום ככולו is a rule that appears in many places in ש״ס, for example in counting days of אבלות and of טומאה.

phrases.english: He holds that part of the day is like the whole day.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings in a general rule about how days are counted
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Day 30 must be fully over before the נזירות ends
steps.terutzMaskana: Once day 30 begins it counts as complete, so shaving on day 30 is valid even for רב מתנא

steps.title: A case where shaving on day 30 does not count
steps.stepSummary: The same משנה says that if someone vowed 'thirty days' and shaved on day 30, it does not count. That seems to go against רב מתנא's rule that part of a day is like the whole day.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: 'I am a נזיר for thirty days.' If he shaved on day 30, it does not count!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב מתנא's answer from another line of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מקצת היום ככולו applies, then a person who vowed thirty days should also finish once day 30 begins. Yet the משנה says shaving on day 30 is not valid.

keyTerms.meaning: I am hereby a נזיר (the vow formula)
He has not fulfilled his obligation

phrases.english: We learned: "I am hereby a nazirite for thirty days,"

phrases.aramaic: אִם גִּילַּח יוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים — לֹא יָצָא!
phrases.english: if he shaved on the thirtieth day, he has not fulfilled his obligation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מתנא's use of מקצת היום ככולו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If part of day 30 counts as the whole day, shaving on day 30 should be valid here too. The משנה says it is not.

steps.title: That case is where he said 'complete' days
steps.stepSummary: The case where day 30 does not count is someone who said 'thirty complete days', so he needs all 30 full days.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is when he said 'complete' days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is speaking about someone who said 'שלימין', complete days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a person says 'complete', he has asked for 30 full days, so the rule of מקצת היום ככולו does not help him. A plain vow without that word still follows רב מתנא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where he says

phrases.english: It is referring to one who says "complete" days.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's case is a plain vow of thirty days, so מקצת היום ככולו should have applied
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is someone who said 'complete' days, so he needs all 30 full days

steps.title: Two נזירויות: shaving on day 31 and day 61
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that someone who took two נזירויות shaves for the first on day 31 and for the second on day 61. This fits רב מתנא well, and the גמרא is setting up a challenge to בר פדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: someone who vowed two נזירויות shaves for the first on day 31 and for the second on day 61. For רב מתנא, that works out fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another line from the same משנה and first shows that it fits רב מתנא. This is a setup line: the challenge to בר פדא comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב מתנא, each נזירות is 30 days. He shaves on day 31, and the second נזירות of 30 days starts that day, so the second shaving lands on day 61. The word בשלמא signals that the next line will say this is hard for the other opinion, בר פדא.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted (it works for one side, but not the other)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop here thinking the step is finished. בשלמא only sets up the contrast, and the actual problem for בר פדא is stated right after this.

phrases.english: We learned: One who vowed two terms of naziriteship

phrases.aramaic: מְגַלֵּחַ אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה יוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים וְאֶחָד,
phrases.english: shaves for the first one on the thirty-first day,
and for the second one on the sixty-first day.
Granted, according to Rav Mattana, it works out well.
phrases.notes: The first shaving day, day 31, is also the first day of the second נזירות, so 30 more days brings him to day 61.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge from another line of the same משנה after the previous challenge was answered
steps.kashyaTarget: בר פדא's view that a plain נזירות is 29 days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The day 31 and day 61 count fits 30-day נזירויות exactly. The next line will argue that it does not fit בר פדא's 29 days.
